title: Mathematical Logic
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is a statement in logic?
cards.a: A declarative sentence that is either TRUE or FALSE, but not both.
cards.hint: Truth value: T (true) or F (false). Exactly one, always.

cards.q: Which sentences are NOT statements?
cards.a: Questions, commands, wishes, exclamations, and open sentences (e.g. x + 3 = 5) with no quantifier.
cards.hint: Trap: 'x + 3 = 5' is a statement only if x is fixed or quantified (∀x / ∃x).

cards.q: Name the 5 logical connectives with symbols.
cards.a: AND: ∧ | OR: ∨ | NOT: ~ (or ¬) | IF–THEN: → | IFF: ↔
cards.hint: ∧ conjunction, ∨ disjunction, → conditional, ↔ biconditional.

cards.q: Truth table rule for p ∧ q?
cards.a: True ONLY when both p and q are T. (TT→T, TF→F, FT→F, FF→F)
cards.hint: Think AND = strict: one F kills it.

cards.q: Truth table rule for p ∨ q?
cards.a: False ONLY when both p and q are F. (TT→T, TF→T, FT→T, FF→F)
cards.hint: Inclusive OR: one T is enough.

cards.q: When is the conditional p → q false?
cards.a: Only when p = T and q = F. (TT→T, TF→F, FT→T, FF→T)
cards.hint: False antecedent ⇒ p → q is always TRUE.

cards.q: When is the biconditional p ↔ q true?
cards.a: When p and q have the SAME truth value. (TT→T, FF→T, TF→F, FT→F)

cards.q: Express p → q using ~ and ∨.
cards.a: p → q ≡ ~p ∨ q
cards.hint: Most used conversion in MHT-CET. Also p → q ≡ ~q → ~p.

cards.q: Negation of p → q?
cards.hint: Trap: the negation of 'if–then' is NOT another 'if–then'. Keep p, negate q, join with ∧.

cards.q: State De Morgan's laws.
cards.hint: Flip the connective AND negate each part.

cards.q: Negation of p ↔ q?
cards.hint: Negating a biconditional gives 'exactly one is true' (XOR).

cards.q: Define tautology, contradiction, contingency.
cards.a: Tautology: always T (last column all T). Contradiction: always F. Contingency: mix of T and F.
cards.hint: Examples: p ∨ ~p is a tautology; p ∧ ~p is a contradiction.

cards.q: Converse, inverse, contrapositive of p → q?
cards.a:
Converse: q → p
Inverse: ~p → ~q
Contrapositive: ~q → ~p
cards.hint: Converse = swap. Inverse = negate both. Contrapositive = swap + negate both.

cards.q: Which of converse/inverse/contrapositive is equivalent to p → q?
cards.a: Only the contrapositive: p → q ≡ ~q → ~p. Converse and inverse are equivalent to EACH OTHER, not to p → q.
cards.hint: Board favourite: write the statement in 'if–then' form first, then convert.

cards.q: Idempotent, commutative and associative laws?
cards.a:
p ∧ p ≡ p, p ∨ p ≡ p
p ∧ q ≡ q ∧ p, p ∨ q ≡ q ∨ p
p ∧ (q ∧ r) ≡ (p ∧ q) ∧ r
p ∨ (q ∨ r) ≡ (p ∨ q) ∨ r
cards.hint: Same pattern holds for both ∧ and ∨.

cards.q: Distributive laws of logic?
cards.hint: Both directions work (unlike ordinary algebra).

cards.q: Identity, complement and involution laws (T = tautology, F = contradiction)?
cards.a:
p ∨ F ≡ p, p ∧ T ≡ p
p ∨ T ≡ T, p ∧ F ≡ F
p ∨ ~p ≡ T, p ∧ ~p ≡ F
~(~p) ≡ p, ~T ≡ F, ~F ≡ T
cards.hint: Complement laws are the key to simplifying switching circuits.

cards.q: What are quantifiers? Give the symbols.
cards.a:
Universal ∀ = 'for all / for every'.
Existential ∃ = 'there exists / for some'.
cards.hint: Quantifiers turn an open sentence into a statement.

cards.q: Negation of quantified statements?
cards.hint: Flip the quantifier AND negate the inside. 'All' ↔ 'Some'.

cards.q: What is the dual of a statement?
cards.a: Interchange ∧ ↔ ∨ and T ↔ F. Keep ~ unchanged. Variables stay the same.
cards.hint: Defined only for statements using ∧, ∨, ~ (and T, F).

cards.q: Find the dual of (p ∧ q) ∨ T.
cards.a: (p ∨ q) ∧ F
cards.hint: Trap: if → or ↔ is present, first rewrite using ∧, ∨, ~, then take the dual.

cards.q: Switching circuits: series, parallel and switch states?
cards.a:
Series ↔ ∧ (p ∧ q). Parallel ↔ ∨ (p ∨ q).
Closed switch = T = 1 (current flows). Open = F = 0.
cards.hint: Series: both must be closed. Parallel: any one closed is enough.

cards.q: Switch p and its complement p' (~p) in series and in parallel?
cards.a:
Series: p ∧ p' ≡ F (never flows).
Parallel: p ∨ p' ≡ T (always flows).
cards.hint: p' is always opposite to p: when p is closed, p' is open.

cards.q: Negate: 'If it rains, then I stay home.'
cards.a: 'It rains AND I do not stay home.' (p ∧ ~q)
cards.hint: Use the negation of p → q. Never write 'if it rains, I don't stay home'.

cards.q: Fastest method to prove A → B is a tautology?
cards.a: Assume A = T and B = F. If this leads to a contradiction, then A → B is a tautology.
cards.hint: Saves time in MCQs compared to a full truth table. Works because p → q is false only for T → F.
